finding: The returning-visitor state is a behaviour the product does not have: on round 2 the code asks for name and email again, so a client who already identified in round 1 never sees 'Welcome back, Sara.'
evidence: Board 113:3 header adds one text node 'Welcome back, Sara.' and is otherwise byte-identical in copy to 23:21. Code: submitReview creates a NEW ReviewRequest row (review.service.ts:64-66) whose data carries no reviewerId; reviewerId is written in exactly two places repo-wide (client-review.service.ts:212, :288), both scoped to the current round. getReviewByToken re-reads review.reviewerId (client-review.service.ts:135-140) and review-client.tsx:182 gates on Boolean(data.reviewer), so round 2 renders the identify form. The Reviewer ROW persists (@@unique([siteId,email]), prisma/schema.prisma:560-575) but the form still appears.
recommend: Either cut 113:3, or keep it and file the code gap: carry reviewerId forward when a new round is created for the same site+email. Do not ship the board as-is; it promises recognition the product does not give.

finding: 125:2 and 125:49 are two full 1280x900 copies of 23:21 that differ in exactly three fills; with 113:3 that makes four complete copies of the landing screen on one page, each free to drift from the others.
evidence: Text dumps of 23:21, 113:3, 125:2 and 125:49 are identical except 113:3's 'Welcome back, Sara.'. Fill probe: 125:2 sets agency name #0f766e, 'brand rule' rect #0f766e, Approve button #0f766e; 125:49 sets agency name #f59e0b, rule #f59e0b, Approve button #1c64f2. Every other fill in both frames matches 23:21. The drift risk is already realised on this page - see D-H-03.
recommend: Reduce the brand pair to one annotated variant of 23:21 (a swatch row plus a callout naming the three tokens that change), rather than two full-screen duplicates.

finding: Three boards on the canonical page are verbatim copies of the page-1:3 ECHO stubs - superseded shell, wrong canvas height - and they duplicate states 121:2 already covers. The echo language has leaked back onto the page the echoes are supposed to defer to.
evidence: 1736:8389/8397/8405 are 1280x720 and carry the header '{Agency}' + 'is asking for your feedback'. All sixteen S5.5 boards are 1280x900 and carry 'Ali's Studio' + 'Reviewing: Bella Cucina · v3'. Body text of 1736:8389 is character-identical to echo 1339:7207 and 1736:8397 to echo 1339:7214. Meanwhile 121:2 ('This link has expired' / 'Ask Ali's Studio for a new link.' / 'Review links work for 90 days.') carries three invisible hotspots 1737:30/34/38 named 'hotspot/state · dead-link · revoked|not-found|conflict', i.e. 121:2 is already the parent of these three states.
recommend: Redraw the three dead-link states as variants of 121:2 in the S5.5 shell at 1280x900, and rename 1736:8389/8397/8405 as superseded rather than leaving two competing designs for one concept on one page.

finding: The expired screen tells a non-user to 'Ask Ali's Studio for a new link' and gives them nothing to ask with - no address, no mailto, no button - and in code that screen cannot even name the agency.
evidence: Board 121:2 text: 'This link has expired' / 'Ask Ali's Studio for a new link.' / 'Review links work for 90 days.'; the frame has no button or link child (geometry probe: card 366x120, three TEXT nodes). Code: the dead-link branch renders <Shell agency="Buildrick"> (review-client.tsx:169) because the query failed and agencyName is unavailable, so the live screen reads 'Buildrick is asking for your feedback'. grep of app/review/ for mailto:, href=, localStorage returns zero matches. TOKEN_TTL_DAYS = 90 (client-review.service.ts:33); no cron touches ReviewRequest.
recommend: Give the expired screen the inviter's email address (it is already on the row as invitedEmail) behind a 'Email Ali's Studio' link, or a 'Request a new link' action that pings the workspace. A dead end with no exit is the one state a non-user cannot self-rescue from.

finding: The transfer-handover expiry board is wired to the REVIEW module's dead-link boards: its three hotspots navigate to 1736:8389/8397/8405, which are client-review token states with an entirely different token, service and audience.
evidence: Reactions on 869:6999: 1736:8412 'hotspot/state · dead-link · revoked' -> 1736:8389; 1736:8416 '... not-found' -> 1736:8397; 1736:8420 '... conflict' -> 1736:8405. The three destination boards say 'Your designer sent an updated link' and 'This round is closed' - review copy. Transfer runs through app/transfer/accept/page.tsx and its own token; client-review.service.ts is not in that path. The hotspot ids 1736:84xx are adjacent to the review dead-link node ids, i.e. the group was duplicated from 121:2 and never re-pointed.
recommend: Remove the three hotspots from 869:6999 or re-point them at transfer-specific states. As drawn, walking the transfer flow lands the reviewer in the review flow.

finding: The only labelled BACK path on two dead-link boards is a cross-page NAVIGATE to an echo stub on page 1:3 - the exact manoeuvre the echo stubs exist because Figma rejects.
evidence: 1736:8389 child 1736:8396 'hotspot/back · Client · A0 identify' -> 1339:7162; 1736:8397 child 1736:8404 same -> 1339:7162. getNodeByIdAsync(1339:7162).parent chain resolves to page 1:3, and its own name reads 'echo of 1:6 (canonical); kept because Figma rejects cross-page NAVIGATE'. 1736:8405 has no back hotspot at all. The frame-level ON_CLICK on all three -> 121:2 is the only in-page path out.
recommend: Re-point both back hotspots at 112:2 (S5.5 · A0 · empty) on this page. A back-link that cannot fire is worse than none: it reads as covered in a flow audit.

screen: Share · expired link / Share · draft preview / Transfer · accept
finding: The share and transfer sub-family is unwalkable: 869:7005 has zero reactions in either direction, and 854:30 and 869:6999 have zero inbound edges, so three of the five boards cannot be reached in the prototype.
evidence: Full reactions sweep of page 1:6 (frame plus every descendant): 854:30 '(NO REACTIONS ANYWHERE)', 869:7005 '(NO REACTIONS ANYWHERE)', 854:41 '(NO REACTIONS ANYWHERE)'. Destination set across the whole page contains 854:41 but never 854:30, 854:35, 869:6999 or 869:7005. 854:35's single edge (854:39 'Button · Accept handover') -> 854:41. So the only walkable transfer path is accept -> accepted; expiry is unreachable from anywhere.
recommend: Wire 854:35 -> 869:6999 as an alternate state hotspot and 854:30 -> 869:7005, the way 112:2 already reaches 121:2 and 121:25. 854:41's terminality is declared in its name and is fine; the two expiry boards are not terminal-by-design, they are unreached.

finding: Both brand-colour boards carry the same frame-level reaction twice, so each has a dead duplicate.
evidence: Reactions sweep: 125:2 has two identical rows 'S5.5 · brand-colour ON_CLICK NODE 125:49 NAVIGATE'; 125:49 has two identical rows '... ON_CLICK NODE 23:21 NAVIGATE'. 125:2 additionally carries 1665:30 'hotspot/alt · S5.5 · brand-colour-fails-contrast' -> 125:49, so the frame-level pair is redundant with the labelled hotspot as well.
recommend: Delete the duplicate frame-level reactions and keep the labelled hotspots.

screen: page furniture - section headers and 20 captions
finding: The page's own navigation furniture describes a layout that no longer exists: the 20 caption labels sit on a different grid from the frames they name, the five section headers undercount the page by three screens, and eight frames have no caption at all.
evidence: Frames are laid out on a 1520px x-pitch at y = 60/1300/2540/3780/5020/6000/6980/7960. Captions 122:51-122:64 + 125:96/125:97 are on a 1380px x-pitch at y = 2016/3016/4016/5016. Concretely: 'caption/S5.5 · A0 · empty' is at (0,2016) while frame 112:2 is at (0,60), and (0,2016) falls inside frame 114:2's box (0..1280, 1300..2200). At y=5016 the captions read load-error / changes-requested / brand-colour / brand-colour-fails-contrast while the frames at y=5020 are 113:3 returning-visitor / 112:21 validation-error / 125:2 / 125:49. Headers: 'Entry & Landing 3 screens' (actual 5), 'Comments & Threads 1 screens', 'Review Flow 1 screens' sits above 854:30 which is the SHARE preview, 'Approve / Reject 1 screens' (actual 2), 'Other States 15 screens' sits above 113:3 which is Entry. Claimed total 21 against 24 frames. No captions exist for the rows at y=6000, 6980, 7960 or for 1736:8389/8397/8405.
recommend: Regenerate the captions and section counts from the frame list rather than hand-maintaining them, and move each caption to 4px above the frame it names, which is the convention the y=5016 row still preserves.

finding: The changes-requested terminal keeps the comment pins on the frozen preview but drops the Comment tab, so the client can see that two notes exist and has no way to open either one - and the sibling terminal, approved, keeps both tabs.
evidence: 122:3 geometry: 'Preview pill' 74x32 is the only tab child of the Branded bar; pins 'pin/1' 24x24 @345,6510 and 'pin/2' 24x24 @911,6510 are drawn on the site preview; the screenshot shows both blue numbered pins with no Comment tab. 117:58 (approved) text dump carries both 'Preview' and 'Comment'. In code neither tab exists at all - review-client.tsx has no Preview/Comment mode switch (grep for Preview|Comment|view-only returns only SitePreview's own page-tab strip at :52-66 and the 'Preview unavailable' string at :44).
recommend: Either drop the pins from 122:3 too, or keep the Comment tab in a read-only mode. Showing a count the client cannot open is the worst of the two.

finding: 122:3 omits the 'Signed as {Name} · {email}' receipt that the code renders on every non-PENDING state and that the sibling terminal 117:58 draws.
evidence: Text dump 117:58 ends '... Signed as Sara Khan · sara@bellacucina.com'; 122:3 ends '... They'll send a new link when the changes are ready.' with no Signed-as node. Code places the Signed-as paragraph outside the approved/changes ternary (review-client.tsx:269-271), so it renders for both branches. This is the surviving half of D-D-06, which claimed both terminals omit it.
recommend: Add the Signed-as line to 122:3's blue bar. It is the client's only receipt that the request was attributed to them.

finding: The approval receipt offers a 'View site' button at the moment the site is by definition not live yet - the same card says 'Ali can now publish it live' - and the control exists in no code path.
evidence: 117:58 card 440x326 contains TEXT 'View site' @612,4304 inside a bordered button, directly under 'Ali can now publish it live.' The frame's only reaction is 117:111 -> 120:2 (post-approval-unchanged), so in the prototype 'View site' returns the client to the same frozen snapshot. Code: the terminal branch (review-client.tsx:250-275) renders heading, one paragraph and the Signed-as line - zero controls; there is no published URL in the getReviewByToken payload (client-review.service.ts:141-173).
recommend: Drop the button, or relabel it to what it can actually do ('See the version you approved') and point it back at the frozen snapshot. Offering 'View site' before publish sets up a 404 or a stale page.

finding: The board tells the returning client that two specific things changed and then shows them the version without the changes, with no way to see what moved - and the number it quotes is not derivable from the code.
evidence: 120:50 warning bar: 'Ali has changed 2 things since you approved.' / 'Your approval still stands. Ali will send a new review only if he needs your sign-off again.' The preview beneath is the same 880x560 snapshot as 23:21. Code: editedSinceApproval is a boolean from a timestamp comparison - site.lastEditedAt > resolvedAt (client-review.service.ts:168-172), same rule as isApprovalStale (publish-approval.ts:58-64). There is no count and no diff anywhere in the review path; changeSummary is designer-typed free text (max 500, schemas/reviews.ts:52-54) and appears on no board. ApprovedCompareView and CompareView are editor-side only.
recommend: Drop the count to what the code can prove ('Ali has made changes since you approved') or build the diff. Quoting '2 things' commits the product to a change feed the client path does not have.

finding: The confirm modal for the one irreversible action in the client's whole experience never says it is irreversible, and three of the four states the code can put it in are unboarded.
evidence: Board 117:2: 'What should Ali fix?' / textarea / '3 pinned comments included' / 'Cancel' / 'Send to Ali'. Code (review-client.tsx:375-463) body copy for the same branch: 'Your note below is sent with this, so your designer knows what to change. This closes the round and you cannot reopen it.' Unboarded: the approve variant ('Approve {site}?' / 'This tells your designer the design is settled and they can put it live.' / 'Not yet' / 'Yes, approve', :378-382,:404-458); the no-note variant ('Your designer will not be told what to change, because you have not written a note.', :387-389); and the in-dialog failure line 'Your note could not be sent, so nothing was submitted' (:390-396). Approve reaches 117:58 directly from 23:21's button 229:1892 with no confirm board in between.
recommend: Board the approve confirm and the no-note variant, and put the 'this closes the round and you cannot reopen it' sentence on 117:2. Per the visual-precedence rule the board wins on copy, so as drawn the board is deleting the only warning the client gets.

finding: Every control on the client's page is sized for a dense internal editor, not for a one-decision public page a non-user opens from an email: the two verdict buttons are 32px, the comment pin is 24x24 and the Post button is 28px.
evidence: Geometry probe (absolute, 1280x900 boards): 'Request changes' INSTANCE 148x32 and Approve 125x32 in the 72px sticky footer (23:21, 114:2, 117:2, 117:58); comment composer input 196x44 with Post 52x28 (114:2 @655,1900); pin/1 24x24 (114:2 @345,1810; 122:3 @345,6510 and @911,6510); identify inputs 340x36 (112:2 @470,418 and @470,496). 44px is the touch-target floor and this is the surface most likely to be opened on a phone - review-client.tsx has zero breakpoints (see D-H-24).
recommend: Take the client page off editor density: 40-44px verdict buttons, a 32px minimum pin hit area, and a Post button no smaller than its input row. The editor's compact density is a rule about the editor.

finding: The client is asked to approve a SITE and is shown one fixed 880x560 crop of one page, with no page navigation and no scroll affordance anywhere in the family - while the code already renders a per-page tab strip the boards never drew.
evidence: Geometry: 'Site preview - view only' 1280x728 containing 'The real built site' 880x560, identical across 23:21, 113:3, 114:2, 117:2, 117:58, 122:3, 120:2, 120:50, 125:2, 125:49. The only tab row on any board is 'Preview | Comment', which is a mode switch, not page navigation; the 'Menu | Book | Find us' row is the customer's own site nav inside the snapshot. Code: SitePreview (review-client.tsx:39-75) renders a tab per snapshot page when pages.length > 1, labelled p.replace(/\.html$/,'').replace(/^index$/,'Home') (:49), over an h-[600px] iframe (:71). The retired echo stub 1339:7171 names the missing part explicitly: its placeholder reads '(the site, page tabs, and Your notes)'.
recommend: Draw the page tab strip on 23:21 and propagate it through the family, and decide whether 560px is a crop or a scaled whole page - as drawn a client approves a site having seen one screenful of one page.

finding: The canonical family designs a comment model the product does not have and drops the one it does: boards show pinned annotations on the site canvas, while the code has a 320px right-hand notes rail and never sends a position.
evidence: Boards: 114:2 draws 'pin/1' 24x24 on a photo opening a 220x132 popover with author 'Sara', the note and a 'Post' button; 122:3 draws pin/1 and pin/2; 117:2 says '3 pinned comments included'. Code: the notes sidebar is <aside className="w-[320px] shrink-0"> with 'Your notes', placeholder "Anything you'd like changed?", maxLength 2000, button 'Add note' (review-client.tsx:322-369). createClientComment accepts pageId/x/y/targetSelector (client-review.service.ts:236-240, schemas/reviews.ts:98-107) but BOTH call sites send only { token, body: draft } (:337, :437), so every comment stores pageId null. The 'Preview | Comment' mode tabs and the 'view-only' chip on every board exist in no code path.
recommend: Decide the model before drawing more states. If pins are the target, the board is a build spec for pageId/x/y wiring that does not exist; if the rail is the target, 114:2 and 122:3 are drawing a feature that will not ship. Right now the file and the product disagree about how a client leaves feedback.

finding: The identify error tells an anonymous visitor on a public URL whether a given address is the one the link was sent to, and it makes the ordinary 'my colleague is reviewing this' case impossible.
evidence: Board 112:21 renders 'That is not the address this link was sent to.' in red under the email field. Code: identifyReviewer throws EMAIL_MISMATCH with exactly that message when normalised !== review.invitedEmail (client-review.service.ts:196-200); exact match only, no plus-addressing tolerance. The route has no session, no middleware (middleware.ts:129 matcher excludes /review), and identify is rate-limited at only 5 per 15 min per IP (routers/client-review.ts:81). Anyone holding the link can test addresses.
recommend: Say 'We could not match that address to this invitation' without confirming or denying, and give the client a way to proceed as a named guest or to have the agency add their address. As drawn the screen is both an enumeration oracle and a dead end for a forwarded link.

finding: Two boards in the transfer family have their primary element orphaned in the top-left corner of the frame, outside the card it belongs to.
evidence: 854:41 screenshot: a filled blue 'Sign in' button sits at roughly (24,92) in the 1440x900 frame while the card at centre reads 'Handover complete' / '"Harbor Dental" now lives in your workspace. Sign in to Buildrick to manage it.' with no button inside it. 869:6999 screenshot: the sentence 'Ask Vortex Studio to send a new invitation.' sits at roughly (24,94) outside the card, and the same sentence already appears inside the card body ('... Ask Vortex Studio to send a new one.').
recommend: Move both children into their cards. This is the auto-layout escape signature - a node added to the frame rather than to the card - and it makes the accepted screen's only action invisible where a reader looks for it.

finding: The board named for a failing brand colour keeps the failing colour on screen: it protects only the CTA and leaves #f59e0b at 2.15:1 on the agency name and the brand rule, and nothing anywhere tells the agency the colour was rejected.
evidence: Fill probe 125:49: TEXT 'Ali's Studio' fill #f59e0b size 14 Medium; RECTANGLE 'brand rule' fill #f59e0b; INSTANCE Button (Approve) fill #1c64f2 - reverted to Buildrik blue. Sibling 125:2 uses #0f766e for all three. Relative luminance of #f59e0b is 0.439, giving 2.15:1 against white; #0f766e is 0.142, giving 5.47:1. AA for 14px normal text needs 4.5:1. Code side: nothing applies an agency colour to this page at all - getReviewByToken selects workspace { name } only (client-review.service.ts:106-116,:147); Workspace.accentColor (prisma/schema.prisma:190) is written by the settings form and read nowhere in server/; the accent is hardcoded #1A56DB at review-client.tsx:236,300,332,349,448; and no contrast function exists in packages/dashboard, server, lib or packages/shared.
recommend: Make the fallback total - when the brand colour fails, drop it from the name and the rule too, not just the button - and add the agency-side state that says why. Both boards are design-ahead of any code, so the rule they encode is the whole specification.

finding: The retry screen's only action is a bare blue text link while every other primary action in the family is a filled button.
evidence: 121:25 screenshot: 'Try again' rendered as plain #1A56DB text at the bottom of a 366x120 card, no border, no fill, no padding box. Compare 112:2 'Start reviewing ->' INSTANCE Button 151x32, 854:35 'Accept handover' filled, 854:41 'Sign in' filled, 117:58 'View site' bordered.
recommend: Make it a button. On the one screen whose entire job is 'press this again', the action should not be the lightest thing on the page.

finding: The loading skeleton does not resemble the layout it precedes: three stacked full-width bars against a centred 880px card with a 56px header and a 72px footer.
evidence: 121:48 screenshot shows blocks of roughly 880x36, 880x140 and 880x96 stacked centrally with 'Opening your review...' beneath. The state it resolves to (23:21, via the AFTER_TIMEOUT reaction on 121:48 -> 23:21) is a 1280x56 branded bar, a 1280x728 preview area holding an 880x560 site card, and a 1280x72 sticky footer.
recommend: Shape the skeleton like the screen: bar, preview block, footer. A skeleton that reflows on load costs more than a spinner.

finding: The public draft-preview screen - the one a prospect actually looks at - is a grey rectangle standing in for the product, with no header, no agency identity and no navigation.
evidence: 854:30 screenshot: a 396x230 flat #F3F4F6 rectangle inside a card, above it only 'Bella Cucina - draft preview' and 'Shared by Vortex Studio · read-only · expires in 14 days'. Compare 23:21, which draws the whole site. Code: app/share/[token]/page.tsx (57 lines) plus password-gate.tsx (95) and not-published.tsx (40) - two further states, neither boarded on this page.
recommend: Draw the actual preview the way 23:21 does, and board the password gate and the not-published state alongside it. As drawn the share family is a placeholder, and D-D-01's original complaint - a white box where the product should be - is true here rather than where it was filed.

screen: Q5 - the client on a phone
finding: There is no mobile board anywhere in the client family, and the code that ships has zero breakpoints and a hard layout floor of roughly 456px, so the one page in the product written for a non-user is the one page that cannot fit a phone.
evidence: All 24 frames on page 1:6 are 1280 or 1440 wide; none is a phone width. review-client.tsx: sm:/md:/lg:/xl: = 0 occurrences, @media|matchMedia|useMediaQuery = 0, flex-col = 5 and all unconditional (:87,:93,:200,:209,:218). The viewing row is <div className="mx-auto flex w-full max-w-[1100px] flex-1 gap-6 p-6"> (:307) holding flex-1 main plus <aside className="w-[320px] shrink-0"> (:322) - 320 + gap-6 + p-6 both sides + main's p-8 is >=456px before content, over a fixed h-[600px] iframe (:71). app/layout.tsx declares no export const viewport, so width=device-width applies and the overflow is real. By contrast transfer/accept adapts, via AuthCard's md: rules (components/auth/auth-card.tsx:12,33,39).
recommend: Board the phone case for at least identify, viewing and the verdict footer, and stack the notes rail below the preview under ~700px. A client who opens the email on a phone is the modal arrival, not the exception.

finding: Leaving notes without giving a verdict is the code's actual default and unlimited, and no board shows it: every canonical viewing board pairs the notes with a live verdict footer, and there is no state for 'you have left three notes and not answered'.
evidence: Code: 'Add note' calls comment.mutate({ token, body: draft }) and nothing else (review-client.tsx:334-352); status stays PENDING; no cap. listClientComments returns every note by that reviewer for that SITE, orderBy createdAt asc (client-review.service.ts:257-270) - so on a re-send the round-1 notes reappear with no round boundary. Boards: 114:2 shows exactly one pin popover with one note; no board on page 1:6 shows a list of two or more notes, a note count, or a 'come back and decide' prompt. No cron touches ReviewRequest, so nothing chases a client who commented and left.
recommend: Board the multi-note list with round separation, and board the state a client returns to after commenting without deciding. This is the most likely real session and it has no design.

screen: Q5 - the verdict failed to submit
finding: There is no board and no code for a failed verdict: resolve.error is never rendered, so a rate-limited or already-resolved submission leaves the modal open, the button re-enabled and the client told nothing.
evidence: grep of resolve. in review-client.tsx: :129 (hook), :292/:299/:447 (disabled), :407/:425 (mutate), :451/:456 (pending labels) - never .error. Contrast comment.error, surfaced twice (:353-355 and the in-dialog line :390-396). resolve runs on strictClientLimit = 5 per 15 min (routers/client-review.ts:81) and resolveReviewByToken can throw ALREADY_RESOLVED (client-review.service.ts:279), which the router maps to CONFLICT (routers/client-review.ts:44-67). The CONFLICT dead-link copy exists (review-client.tsx:29-32) but is unreachable, which board 1736:8405's own name already records.
recommend: Board the failure line inside the confirm modal, mirroring the note-failed line the code already has, and render resolve.error. Silently swallowing the failure of the one irreversible action is the worst available outcome.

finding: Two shipped states of the share route have no board on the client page: the password gate and the not-published screen.
evidence: packages/dashboard/app/share/[token]/password-gate.tsx (95 lines, client component) and not-published.tsx (40 lines), plus the POST route app/api/share/[token]/verify-password/route.ts (93 lines). Page 1:6 carries only 854:30 (draft preview) and 869:7005 (expired link); text dumps of both contain no password or unpublished copy.
recommend: Board both. A password-protected share link is a prospect's first contact with the agency and it currently ships undesigned.

finding: The handover screen offers only 'Accept handover'. There is no way to decline, in the board or in the code, so the recipient's only two possible answers are one button and closing the tab.
evidence: 854:35 text dump: 'Accept site handover' / 'Vortex Studio is transferring "Harbor Dental" to you. Accepting moves the site into your workspace.' / 'Accept handover' - one button, one reaction (854:39 -> 854:41). grep of decline|Decline|reject|Reject|No thanks|Cancel across app/transfer/accept/page.tsx and server/services/*transfer* returns zero matches. The copy also presumes 'your workspace' with no board for a recipient who has no Buildrik account.
recommend: Add a decline action and its confirmation, and board the no-account arrival. Silence is currently indistinguishable from refusal, and the sending agency learns nothing either way.

screen: Q5 - the designer's note is fetched and never shown
finding: The boards put the designer's ask in the footer of every viewing state; the code fetches that field and renders it nowhere, so the client sees the site with no idea what they were asked to look at.
evidence: Board footer on 23:21, 113:3, 114:2, 117:2, 117:58, 125:2, 125:49: 'Ali asks: "homepage + menu ready - approve when happy"'. Code: getReviewByToken selects and returns note (client-review.service.ts:98,:149); grep for data.note in review-client.tsx returns zero matches. The note reaches the client only in the invite email (emails/review-invite.tsx:54-59), which they may have opened days earlier.
recommend: Render data.note in the sticky footer exactly as the boards draw it. The board is already the fix; the code just never picked it up.

screen: Q5 - a transient failure reads as a broken link
finding: Board 121:25 designs the right thing and the code cannot reach it: every clientReview.get failure falls through to the NOT_FOUND copy, so a 500 or a dropped connection tells the client their link is broken and to stop trying.
evidence: Board 121:25: 'We couldn't open this right now.' / 'Nothing is wrong with your link. Try again in a moment.' / 'Try again'. Code: const copy = DEAD_LINK_COPY[reason ?? ""] ?? DEAD_LINK_COPY[code] ?? DEAD_LINK_COPY.NOT_FOUND with code = review.error.data?.code ?? "NOT_FOUND" (review-client.tsx:165-167). An INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR matches no key, so the client is shown 'This link doesn't work' / 'It may have been copied incompletely. Try clicking the link in your email again rather than pasting it.' (:25-28). The query is created with retry: false (:126), and there is no retry control anywhere in the file.
recommend: Add a transient branch keyed on INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR / TIMEOUT / network failure, rendering 121:25's copy with a refetch button. Telling a client their link is broken when the server hiccuped ends the review round for no reason.

screen: Q4 - the header subtitle the boards specify vs the one the code renders
finding: Every canonical board specifies the header subtitle 'Reviewing: {Site} · v{n}'; the code hardcodes 'is asking for your feedback' on every branch and substitutes literals for the agency name, producing 'Loading is asking for your feedback' and 'Buildrick is asking for your feedback'.
evidence: All sixteen S5.5 boards carry 'Ali's Studio' + 'Reviewing: Bella Cucina · v3' - verified by text dump on 112:2, 23:2, 112:21, 113:3, 23:21, 114:2, 117:2, 117:58, 122:3, 120:2, 120:50, 121:2, 121:25, 121:48, 125:2, 125:49. screen: Q3 - echo stubs have drifted from the screens they echo
finding: All six echo stubs on page 1:3 have drifted wholesale from their canonicals on 1:6 - different shell, different canvas size, different copy, and in two cases a different product behaviour - so the editor prototype teaches screens that do not exist.
evidence: Six pairs, all verified by text dump. 1339:7162 vs 112:2: zero strings in common; the echo has no form fields, its CTA is 'Look at {Site}', the canonical's is 'Start reviewing ->'. 1339:7171 vs 23:21: echo is a placeholder box '(the site, page tabs, and Your notes)' with buttons 'Request changes'/'Approve this design'; canonical draws the site with '✓ Approve v3'. 1340:7162 vs 114:2: echo draws a 'Your notes' rail with 'Add note'; canonical draws in-canvas pins with 'Post' - two different comment models. 1339:7186 vs 117:58: echo is plain text with no receipt; canonical is a success modal with timestamp, 'Signed as Sara Khan · sara@bellacucina.com' and 'View site'. 1339:7193 vs 122:3: echo says '...ready for you', canonical '...ready'; echo has ZERO reactions, canonical has hotspot/back 444:4041. 1340:7174 vs 120:50: echo says 'If you were sent a new link, use that one', canonical says 'Your approval still stands. Ali will send a new review only if he needs your sign-off again' - contradictory instructions to the same client. All echoes are 1280x720; all canonicals are 1280x900.
recommend: Regenerate the six echoes from their canonicals in one pass, or reduce each to a labelled 200x100 stub that says 'see 1:6 node <id>' and carries only the NAVIGATE. A half-drawn stub is safe; a drifted full drawing is not, and this drift already leaked back onto 1:6 as 1736:8389/8397/8405.

screen: Q4 - consent on the screen that collects the client's name and email
finding: No board on page 1:6 draws the cookie banner, including the one screen that collects a name and email from a person with no account - and the sticky footer's banner-offset state is therefore unspecified.
evidence: Text dumps of all 24 frames on page 1:6 contain no cookie copy. CookieConsent is mounted globally via GlobalProviders (app/layout.tsx:69, components/global/global-providers.tsx:11) and there is no layout.tsx under app/review, so it renders on /review/[token]. The code already compensates for it: the sticky footer is style={{ bottom: "var(--cookie-inset, 0px)" }} (review-client.tsx:105-106) against the banner's fixed z-[9998] (components/global/cookie-consent.tsx:142), which publishes its measured height at :94. This is D-D-07 re-grounded on the canonical page; the specific 'covers the Approve buttons' risk is already solved, the unboarded part is the offset footer.
recommend: Draw the banner on 112:2 and on one viewing board with the footer raised by var(--cookie-inset), so the raised footer is a designed state rather than a computed one.

screen: Q3 - a board named TERMINAL that links back to the pending screen
finding: Four resolved-state boards carry a back hotspot to 23:21, the PENDING screen, which the client can no longer reach - and one of them declares itself terminal in its own name.
evidence: 122:3 is named '... TERMINAL by design - the branch renders text + Signed as, zero controls' and carries 444:4041 'hotspot/back · S5.5 · landing-viewing' -> 23:21. Same on 120:2 (1665:34), 120:50 (444:4039) and 125:49 (1665:32). Code: once status !== PENDING the terminal branch renders and the preview and footer are gone (review-client.tsx:250-275), so there is no product path back to the pending view.
recommend: Keep the hotspots if they are prototype-walk conveniences, but name them 'hotspot/walk' rather than 'hotspot/back' so a flow audit does not count them as product edges - D-D-04's zero-outbound reading was correct and these four edges obscure it.

screen: Q5 - the agency is never told the client acted
finding: Nothing tells the agency the client answered, on any surface, and no board on this page acknowledges that - the client's terminal screens promise a designer who will act, and no signal reaches that designer.
evidence: resolveReviewByToken (client-review.service.ts:273-293) does one prisma.reviewRequest.update and returns; the file's only imports are node:crypto and @/lib/prisma, and it contains no notify/sendEmail/logAuditEvent/webhook call. notifyReviewSubmitted and notifyReviewResolved are module-private async functions in review.service.ts, called only at :111 (submitReview, protectedProcedure + requireAgencyLayer + EDITOR role) and :481 (resolveReview, admin path). No review-related createNotification exists. Board copy that assumes otherwise: 117:58 'Ali can now publish it live.', 122:3 'Your notes are with your designer. They'll send a new link when the changes are ready.' This confirms D-D-04 against the canonical boards.
recommend: Send the agency an email and an in-app notification from resolveReviewByToken. Every terminal screen on this page makes a promise on the designer's behalf that the system does not deliver.
